messages:
jess (support): Heads-up — escalation from Acme. They upgraded to rdx-2.10 yesterday and their structured-output responses are coming back with missing object keys and turned-to-null fields. Example: `user_profile` used to have `email`/`plan` but now email is null and `subscriptionState` is 0 instead of 'ACTIVE'. Customer blocked in prod. request_id: req_0x9f1a. Please triage.

ken (applied-ml): Can you paste a minimal repro (prompt + model params) and the raw response body? Also which exact model variant? rdx-2.10 or rdx-2.10-quant?

jess (support): They called `rdx-2.10` (hosted). Repro below — payload and two outputs (expected vs actual).

jess (support): ```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "rdx-2.10",
  "input": "Extract a JSON user_profile from the text:\nUser: Jane Doe, jane@example.com, plan: pro, status: active",
  "response_format": "json",
  "schema": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "user_profile": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "name": {"type": "string"},
          "email": {"type": "string"},
          "plan": {"type": "string"},
          "subscriptionState": {"type": "string"}
        },
        "required": ["name","email","plan","subscriptionState"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

jess (support): Expected body (what customer historically received):
```json
{"user_profile": {"name": "Jane Doe", "email": "jane@example.com", "plan": "pro", "subscriptionState": "ACTIVE"}}
```

jess (support): Actual body returned from rdx-2.10 (raw):
```json
{"user_profile": {"name": "Jane Doe", "email": null, "plan": "pro", "subscriptionState": 0}}
```

ken (applied-ml): Huh. Enum encoded as int and email nullified. Do we have the tokenization/decoder logs for req_0x9f1a? Could be a change in the structout normalizer or streaming chunk joiner. Also, was there any automatic fallback to a quantized variant?

morgan (infra): No fallback noted; request hit hosted-pool-us-west-1 on gpu-node g-12. I pulled the request trace:

morgan (infra): ```
trace: req_0x9f1a -> srv-host-17 -> model-runner rdx-2.10 -> structout-normalizer v1.4 -> response-proxy
status: 200
latency_ms: 85
```

ken (applied-ml): Can you dump the model-runner stdout segment for that call (we want the pre-normalizer generation token stream)? Need to see whether the model generated the correct strings or if the normalizer mutated them.

jess (support): Pasted the pre-normalizer content (trimmed):
```
{"generated_text":"{\"user_profile\": {\"name\": \"Jane Doe\", \"email\": \"jane@example.com\", \"plan\": \"pro\", \"subscriptionState\": \"ACTIVE\"}}"}
```

ken (applied-ml): OK — model generated correct json. So the regression is after generation. That implicates structout-normalizer or a serialization step. Morgan, any deploys to normalizer or proxy in the window?

morgan (infra): There was a small change 2 hours before the incident — puppet bump: structout-normalizer v1.4.1 -> v1.4.2. Changelog: "handle numeric enum normalization more aggressively" — hmm.

ken (applied-ml): That explains enum remapping ("ACTIVE" -> 0) but not nulling email. Could 1.4.2 have a bug where quoted strings that match email regex are being masked for PII and replaced with null when a schema rule flags them? Check normalization rules.

morgan (infra): Found the normalization rule that applies PII redaction when the schema type is not explicitly `string` in the normalizer config. A regression introduced a default strictness flag that toggles PII masking if the schema is inferred vs explicit. In our call, the schema was explicit but the normalizer saw `response_format: json` and then attempted to coerce types, misdetecting `email` as non-string due to quoting edge-case in the token joiner.

ken (applied-ml): Repro locally by running the normalizer binary on the pre-normalizer payload. I ran: `./structout-normalizer --input sample.json --rules v1.4.2` and got the same transformation. So bug confirmed.

ken (applied-ml): Immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back structout-normalizer to v1.4.1 in hosted pools (fast rollback), 2) apply a hotfix that disables the strictness flag, 3) advise customer to pin to model variant `rdx-2.9` or set a response_normalization param to `legacy` (if available). Customer wants rollback.

jess (support): Customer asked for rollback -> can we do fast rollback across hosted-us-west? They're on a time-sensitive campaign.

morgan (infra): Initiating rollback job now. Deploy-bot will post updates.

deploy-bot: Starting deployment: rollback structout-normalizer -> v1.4.1 across pool hosted-pool-us-west-1. Job id: job_4521. ETA ~2m. :hourglass: 

morgan (infra): Rollback applied to 50% of nodes, ramping. Monitoring logs for transformations.

morgan (infra): Rollback complete on pool. Verified with the same request replay: output from normalizer now matches expected.

jess (support): Verified with Acme on a test call — they see the expected JSON now. Customer is rolling forward and wants a postmortem and timeline. They also want a patch so we can re-enable the stricter normalization safely.

ken (applied-ml): I'll open a PR to fix the strictness toggling (ensure schema explicitness is respected and PII redaction uses type annotations only). Will add regression tests (token-join edgecases + email patterns).

jess (support): Thanks team. I'll notify customer and create an incident ticket for follow-up. cc @ken @morgan :pray: 

morgan (infra): Filed incident INC-2024-291. Adding timeline and logs.

jess (support): Follow-up: customer asked for the earliest date we can re-enable the stricter normalizer with a safe rollout and a feature-flag. Ken, can you estimate?

ken (applied-ml): Give me ~48h to get tests and a hotfix. Then we can do canary with `response_normalization=strict` behind a flag.

jess (support): Great. Closing the escalation for now; will update the ticket with the rollback notes and next steps. :white_check_mark:
